candidates.title: FNet: Mixing Tokens with Fourier Transforms
candidates.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
candidates.abstract: We show that Transformer encoder architectures can be sped up, with limited accuracy costs, by replacing the self-attention sublayers with simple linear transformations that “mix” input tokens. Most surprisingly, we find that replacing the self-attention sublayer in a Transformer encoder with a standard, unparameterized Fourier Transform achieves 92-97% of the accuracy of BERT counterparts on the GLUE benchmark, but trains 80% faster on GPUs and 70% faster on TPUs at standard 512 input lengths. At longer input lengths, our FNet model is significantly faster: when compared to the “efficient Transformers” on the Long Range Arena benchmark, FNet matches the accuracy of the most accurate models, while outpacing the fastest models across all sequence lengths on GPUs (and across relatively shorter lengths on TPUs). Finally, FNet has a light memory footprint and is particularly efficient at smaller model sizes; for a fixed speed and accuracy budget, small FNet models outperform Transformer counterparts.
candidates.reason: Transformer encoderのself-attentionをparameter-free Fourier mixingへ置換し、FFTのO(N log N)性と小memory footprintで推論を直接高速化する。BERT-Base比で8×V100 GPUのinference 82ms→46ms（1.8x）、TPU 32ms→23ms（1.4x）を報告し、長系列でもefficient Transformer群より高速なため対象。
candidates.library_body_check: fulltext_relevance_review: arXiv一次HTML本文§1,§3,§4.1を確認。sequence/hidden dimensionへ2D DFTを適用してattention sublayerを完全置換し、GPUでは512–8192 tokensでFFTを使用。Table 3でbatch 64/8 V100のBERT-Base inference 82msに対しFNet-Base 46ms (1.8x)、4×4 TPU v3では32ms→23ms (1.4x)、forward GFLOPs 98→62を確認。
